bayts.text: You have triumphed through grace in good deeds, mistress of virtuous women; O Maryam, you have surpassed the women of certain faith with Him Who is beyond (all) grasp.
“Be, and it is” led to you the best of messengers (ʿĪsā), beyond objection; and through you whoever holds right belief and is no associator has triumphed.
It is not hidden from the believers that you are the beloved of those who submit, O mother of the best of those who do good, preserved from the snare (of sin).
What has been told of you, by grace, leads me to your praise: you have triumphed with a gladness that makes every God-fearing one of understanding smile.
I have turned to you today with that which makes a nourishment endure for me, with that (which leads me) to the possession of cool water, without pretending to reach (your full merit).
You are the lineage of the noble; nothing unlawful has come near you; and you are worthy of reverence, without turning toward the snares.
Our Lord, the Generous, has appreciated your state with an appreciation that never ceases; your son (ʿĪsā) has attained what he desires with Him Who is beyond grasp.
By this, out of love for you, I have sought a good pleasure that makes your nearness everlasting, from the Lord of the heaven of orbits (Qurʾān 51:7), Giver of guidance and of worship.
By Allah, Lord of “Be, and it is”, I have asked Him that my poem be a support for you, and that He make my worship good.

O mother of the Spirit of the King (ʿĪsā, Spirit of Allah), O mother of him who lights up the dark (night): your son has not perished, (he is) with the Most High, He Who holds back (Qurʾān 4:157-158).
The Possessor of Majesty has blessed you, and your son who banishes straying, through that by which the lawful is made everlasting for the reader who holds fast to it.
Accept my gift without refusal, just as it was accepted (Qurʾān 3:37), with a Generous One Who accepted, (the vow) of your blessed forebear.
